nodes.name: Notify webhook
nodes.notes: The app POSTs one event per state change. Raw body is required: the signature is computed over the exact bytes, so re-serialising the JSON would change them and every request would fail verification.

nodes.name: Verify signature
nodes.notes: Fails CLOSED on a bad or missing signature (throws, which n8n reports as a failed execution) and reads KOYA_NOTIFY_SECRET the same way koya-proposal-delivery.json reads its webhook secret in 3/build: $env first, $vars second, because touching a blocked $env THROWS rather than returning undefined and would otherwise kill this node before the fail-closed branch runs.

nodes.name: Route by level
nodes.notes: Two channels, deliberately separated. A success feed gets skimmed; an error feed gets read. Mixing them is how an error stops being noticed.

nodes.name: Discord #content-errors
nodes.notes: The webhook URL lives in this credential (n8n → Credentials → Discord Webhook), not in a workflow variable and not in this node's parameters. Same posture as 3/build/n8n/koya-proposal-delivery.json's Discord nodes: the URL never appears in the workflow's own JSON, in an execution log, or in a Variables list an admin can browse — only inside the encrypted credential store.

nodes.name: Email via Gmail
nodes.notes:
PRIMARY EMAIL LANE, and it is Gmail rather than Resend for one practical reason: Resend will only deliver to arbitrary recipients from a VERIFIED DOMAIN. Without one its shared onboarding@resend.dev sender can reach the account owner and nobody else, so every notification addressed to anyone outside this project was accepted by the API and silently never arrived. An assessor would have received nothing.

Gmail sends as the connected account, needs no domain, and costs nothing. Connect it under Credentials, Gmail OAuth2.

The error output falls through to the Resend node, so a Gmail outage still gets the mail out where a domain IS configured.

nodes.name: Email via Resend
nodes.notes:
SECOND LANE INSIDE n8n, reached only from the Gmail node's error output.

It needs a VERIFIED DOMAIN on the Resend account to reach anyone but the account owner, which is exactly why it is no longer first. Where a domain exists it is the better sender; where one does not, it silently delivers nothing, and silence is the failure mode this project exists to avoid.

The key lives in n8n's CREDENTIAL STORE as HTTP Header Auth, Authorization: Bearer re_…, never in this node body and never in the app's environment.

The app keeps a Resend key of its own for a THIRD lane, used only when this whole workflow is unreachable. If that one fires, the email says so, because a reader who gets the mail but no Discord message should know why.

nodes.name: Acknowledge
nodes.notes: The app treats a non-2xx as 'n8n lane failed' and falls back to sending the email itself. So this must respond only after the fan-out has been attempted — acknowledging early would make the fallback unreachable.
